behavior_in_task_description.explanation: The instruction asks the agent to fix every way the released coins misbehave in the attached recording, and it states the water requirement in measurable terms: coins sink slowly no matter how hard they hit the surface, taking about 2 s to go from block height to the floor. The water tests check exactly that (a coin dropped fast into the water stays above the floor through 1.6 s; a coin starting at rest in the water keeps sinking slowly). The burst tests (coins thrown to both sides, the whole burst comes down, landed coins stop instead of sliding) are not spelled out in words. They are, however, the visible symptoms in the recording, which this multimodal task makes the primary specification, and they match normal coin behaviour.

behavior_in_tests.explanation: All three wrong behaviours shown in the recording have their own behavioural tests run in the real game binary: water sinking (floats_in_water_by_1s, still_sinking_at_1_6s, sinks_slowly_from_rest), the burst spreading to both sides and releasing every coin (scatters_to_both_sides, releases_full_burst), and landed coins coming to rest (landed_coins_come_to_rest). There are also pass-to-pass sanity checks.

informative_test_structure.explanation: evaluate_heavycoin.py opens with a docstring describing both test levels and their geometry and zones. Each test has a descriptive ID and a detailed failure message. The test.sh run_tests block is commented. The rest of test.sh and verifier.py is standard harness code with explanatory comments.

anti_cheating_measures.explanation: The bug patches are applied and deleted within the same layer. The upstream git history is dropped, so the fix commit cannot be reached. All file timestamps are set to the same value so the newest file does not point to the bug. Tests and solution are not in the image. The agent runs without network. The verifier restores the test paths and judges by running the game, not by reading source, so string matching gives no shortcut.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task is a source-code bug fix. It asks for no structured output.

pinned_dependencies.explanation: SuperTux is checked out at a fixed commit and its submodules are initialised at that commit. Only apt packages from the Ubuntu 24.04 base are used, which do not need pinning. No pip packages are installed.

typos.explanation: No typos were found in paths, commands, test IDs or file names. The IDs agree across task.toml, config.json and evaluate_heavycoin.py. test.sh keeps a few stale comments about a wx in-tree build copied from a template; they are harmless and affect nothing.

tests_or_solution_in_image.explanation: The Dockerfile copies only ca-certificates.crt, the bug patches (deleted in the same layer) and recording.mp4. Neither tests/ nor solution/ is copied in.

test_deps_in_image.explanation: The image contains only the build toolchain, the game's libraries and ffmpeg/xvfb for inspecting the video. The tests need just the game binary and python3's standard library, so no test-only dependencies are baked in.

hardcoded_solution.explanation: solve.sh applies a real source patch that fixes all three defects (the mirrored velocity axis, water physics with a cap on drop speed, and zeroing velocity on landing). It does not write out expected outputs.

file_reference_mentioned.explanation: The agent fixes existing source files and creates no output files. The only file it needs to know about, the recording, is named in the instruction together with its path.
